title: He Shouldn’t Have Been Chosen… So Why Did God Pick Him?
paragraphs:
He Shouldn’t Have Been Chosen… So Why Did God Pick Him?
Why God Often Uses the Least Qualified—and Why That Might Be You
He was the last one anyone would have called.
Not the strongest. Not the most impressive. Not even the one his own father thought was worth bringing to the lineup.
When the prophet came, they didn’t even mention his name.
They forgot him.
Or maybe… they never thought he mattered.
And yet, heaven already knew.
Because while people were measuring outward strength, God was searching for something deeper… something hidden… something raw.

“כִּ֤י הָאָדָם֙ יִרְאֶ֣ה לַעֵינַ֔יִם וַיהוָ֖ה יִרְאֶ֥ה לַלֵּבָֽב”
“For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.” (1 Samuel 16:7)
That word “לַלֵּבָב” (lalevav)… it doesn’t just mean “heart” like emotion.
It means the inner core… the hidden seat of will, desire, truth… who you really are when no one is watching.
David was overlooked by men… but fully seen by God.
And that’s where everything begins to shift.
Because God has always had this pattern… this scandalous, upside-down way of choosing people.
Moses stuttered.

“לֹ֤א אִישׁ֙ דְּבָרִ֣ים אָנֹ֔כִי”
“I am not a man of words…” (Exodus 4:10)
Gideon hid in fear.
“My clan is the weakest… and I am the least…” (Judges 6:15)
Peter was impulsive, unstable… the kind of man who could swear loyalty one minute and deny Jesus the next.

“οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον”
“I do not know the man.” (Matthew 26:74)
Paul… was a persecutor.
Not just lost… but violently opposed to Christ.
So why would God choose people like this?
Why not the polished… the prepared… the impressive?
Because what qualifies you in the eyes of the world often disqualifies you from dependence on God.
And God is not looking for perfection.
He is looking for surrender.
The Greek word “χάρις” (charis)—grace—means unearned favor.
Not improved favor.
Not deserved favor.
Unearned.
Which means if you think you’re too broken… too inconsistent… too far gone…
You are exactly the kind of person grace was designed for.
And that’s the part many people don’t want to admit.
Because it confronts pride.
It strips control.
It forces honesty.
You don’t get to bring your résumé to God.
You bring your repentance.

“μετανοεῖτε” (metanoeite)
Repent.
Not just feel bad… but turn… change direction… surrender your way for His.
That’s where the real transformation begins.
Not when you fix yourself.
But when you finally stop pretending you can.
Be honest… this hit deeper than you expected.
Because maybe you’ve been disqualifying yourself.

Telling yourself:
“I’m not ready.”
“I don’t know enough.”
“I’ve messed up too many times.”
But God has never waited for someone to be “ready.”
He calls… and then He makes them ready.
That’s the scandal.
That’s the grace.
From the outside, it looks irrational.
From heaven, it’s intentional.

“ἀρκεῖ σοι ἡ χάρις μου”
“My grace is sufficient for you…” (2 Corinthians 12:9)
Sufficient.
Enough.
Not lacking.
Not almost.
Enough.
So the question isn’t whether you’re qualified.
The real question is…
Are you willing?
Because the same God who chose David from the field… Moses from the desert… Peter from failure… Paul from darkness…
Is still calling people today.
Not the ones who have it all together.
But the ones who are finally honest enough to admit they don’t.
Someone you know needs this.
Send it to them.
There are people silently disqualifying themselves right now… and this might be the moment God interrupts that lie.
Because you will need to come back to this on the days when your past feels louder than God’s calling.
And if you feel something pulling you deeper… not just inspired, but convicted… not just emotional, but awakened…
Then don’t stay at the surface.
Follow.
Stay close to truth.
Because discipleship isn’t a moment… it’s a daily surrender.
And if you truly want to glorify God—not just feel encouraged for a moment but actually grow, actually change, actually walk with Christ—
Then support what is feeding your spirit.
It’s choosing to invest in truth over distraction.
It’s choosing growth over comfort.
If your soul is hungry… don’t ignore it.
Because the truth is…
God is not looking for the most qualified.
He’s looking for the most surrendered.
And sometimes…
the person you’ve been disqualifying…
is the very person He’s calling.
